verticalReference.evidence: OS local correction TQ3883/TQ3983 and 2003 crest comparison. Historic Liverpool attribution and benchmark identity remain conditional; this is not a survey calibration.

parameters.method: Fill and spill over a depression hierarchy (flood_basins.py, docs/lib/flood-volume.js). Rain: the storm total on each hollow's whole catchment, no losses. Tide and river: weir flow Q = C x 2 m x (h - saddle)^1.5 summed over every 2 m cell edge of the crest a basin shares with the water (or with ground already holding the source), free overfall, integrated over the tide curve or the held duration; water stands above the crest up to the source level and the rest returns. Sluices: their discharge while the water outside is below the sill, for each tide of the duration.

estimates.weirCoefficient: Broad-crested weir over grass banks; 1.7 is the ideal value, 1.6 allows for an uneven crest. Free overfall overstates inflow once the basin fills.
estimates.sluiceDischargeM3PerSecond: About a 0.6 m culvert under 0.5 m of head (0.68 m³/s ideal), reduced for flap, silt and weed. Not surveyed.
estimates.sillODN: The lowest drawn ground within 16 m of the mapped sluice (the ditch bed). Not surveyed.

scenarios.description: Scenario presets for the volume flood view (FLOOD_MODEL_PLAN.md section 4.6, Phase V). Every total is an estimate chosen to illustrate a mechanism, not a measured event. Levels are ODN metres; the surge is the rise of high water above ordinary high water (Trinity High Water, os-tide-levels.json).

riverLevelODN.note: Held level on the non-tidal water (the Lea above the locks, the upper Channelsea and the other reaches outside the tide polygons). The default is the model's retained datum, 0.06 m scene (tide_levels.RETAINED). Phase 2 replaces this with pound levels from the Lea flow.

presets.label: Winter storm, high tides (estimate)

presets.evidence: Illustrative. The surge is a modest spring-tide-plus-wind rise, well below the 1928 peak.

presets.label: Surge to the 1928 height (one tide)
presets.caption: High water about 5.1 m ODN, the 1928 peak near Bow, on the 1890s ground for one tide. The 1928 walls and ground were not those of the 1890s.

presets.label: River held high for a day (estimate)
presets.caption: The non-tidal reaches held at 3.4 m ODN for a day with 20 mm of rain. The level is an estimate until Phase 2 computes the pounds from the Lea flow.

limitations: Geometric connected inundation, not a flow or event simulation: no speed, timing, rainfall, mill operation or ponding on recession (FLOOD_MODEL_PLAN.md phases 2-4).

The Thames and a 30 m band along its shore are the closed edge of the model: the regional marsh has no Thames river wall east of Bow Creek (its ground runs at about 1.8-1.9 m ODN to the water), so the tide enters only up Bow Creek. This assumes the Thames wall held.
Land figures exclude every mapped water polygon (tidal or not).
One source so far: the tidal reaches at a single test level. The back rivers above Three Mills are still tidal in the model; the mill ponds and the Navigation come in Phase 2.
Water stops at the edge of the modelled ground (the regional landscape envelope); stageTable.modelEdgeCells counts wet cells there.
Most ground and bank heights remain scene interpretations; only the old box carries the historic support field.
Two-metre cells keep the highest one-metre sample, broadening narrow barriers slightly. The regional grid shows the lowest level of each 10 m block.
Buildings remain visible; indoor flooding is not calculated. Heights use the provisional ODN reference.
